“I should be the team leader,” Anand said. “I've done three inter-school quizzes.”

“You also talk over everyone,” said Tanuja.

“That's not the point.”

“It is the point, Anand. Last time you took credit for my science answer.”

“I said ‘we’ answered it!”

“You said ‘I’.”

Sunita, at the end of the bench, looked at her shoes. Kabir mumbled, “Can we just get on with practice?”

“No,” said Tanuja. “I'm tired of reading the questions while you decide the answers.”

Anand paused. “I... didn't realise it felt like that. I just want people to know I worked hard.”

“Then say ‘we’ in front of the teacher,” said Tanuja. “And let me lead the science round.”

qa.q: How many inter-school quizzes had Anand done?
qa.a: Anand had done three inter-school quizzes.

qa.q: What was Anand really wanting in demanding to be the leader?
qa.a: Anand wanted recognition for the hard work, and underneath the demand was a wish for respect.

qa.q: What did Tanuja ask Anand to do at the end?
qa.a: Tanuja asked Anand to say “we” in front of the teacher and let Tanuja lead the science round.

qa.q: How might Sunita feel sitting at the end of the bench looking at her shoes?
qa.a: Sunita probably feels uncomfortable and unsure whether to speak, wishing the argument would end.

grounding: Teenagers on a team clash over who leads and who gets credit, and the fight is about respect and recognition more than the task.

passage:
I'm Pradeep, and in Class 9 our robotics team nearly fell apart over who would present. Deepak had built the base, I had written the code, and Karan had designed the arm. The night before the fair, Deepak said, “I'll present. It's my robot.” I said, “It's our robot, and my code makes it move.” We shouted for ten minutes about a two-minute speech. Karan sat between us saying nothing.

Looking back, I don't think it was about the speech. I wanted the teacher to see that I mattered. Deepak, I now think, wanted the same. In the end our teacher split the presentation into three parts, and that took the air out of the fight.

qa.q: What was Pradeep really feeling behind the shouting?
qa.a: Pradeep felt insecure and wanted the teacher to see that Pradeep mattered, so the fight was about recognition more than the speech.

qa.q: What choice by the teacher ended the fight?
qa.a: The teacher split the presentation into three parts so each person spoke.

qa.q: What might Karan have felt sitting silently between the two?
qa.a: Karan probably felt uncomfortable and overlooked, unsure whether to side with anyone, while the arm design was not mentioned.

grounding: Teenagers on a team clash over who presents and who gets credit, and looking back the fight was about respect and recognition.
